# UMC: dated foundry operating-assets study
**Research cutoff:** 19 October 2026. **Capital anchor:** 30 June 2026. **Model currency:** New Taiwan dollars. This is a dated conditional operating-assets valuation, excluding the nonoperating equity portfolio. It is not a current target or a complete total-company fair value.

## Eligibility and security
United Microelectronics is in the original Atlas inventory (sectors 4 and 5). It is a Taiwan issuer with a US-listed, Robinhood-supported NYSE ADS, ticker UMC, rather than a foreign-only security. One ADS represents **five ordinary shares**. Taiwan ordinary stock is TWSE 2303; do not use the Taiwan quote as an ADS price. [Issuer Q2 announcement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322027/umc-ex99.htm), [Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/UMC/).

The June share reconciliation is 12,576,984,870 issued ordinary shares less 30,551,000 treasury shares = **12,546,433,870 outstanding ordinary shares**. Already-issued employee restricted shares are included; adding the same awards again would double count. The number of ADSs actually deposited is not the denominator for the whole company: ordinary equity first divides by all outstanding ordinary shares, then multiplies by five. The exact issued/treasury evidence and later cancellations are in `capital-claims/`.

A June 30 closing exchange rate of **NT$31.837 per US$1** converts the resulting TWD value to USD per ADS. This is the central bank's dated spot rate, not the Q2 income-statement average of 31.59 and not October FX. `fx-ads-v1.json` preserves the exact source row and hash. [Central Bank closing rates, dated row](https://www.cbc.gov.tw/en/lp-700-2-2-60.html).

## What the business earns
UMC manufactures chips for fabless and integrated-device customers. Its current wafer-sales mix is concentrated in specialty/mature nodes rather than frontier processor fabrication. In Q2 2026, 22/28nm contributed 37% of wafer sales; the next node band through 40nm contributed 15%, and the 40–65nm band 18%. No revenue from 14nm-and-below is shown in that mix. Communications, consumer, computer and other applications represented 39%, 32%, 13% and 16%. Asia-Pacific customers represented 66%, North America 22%, Europe 8%, Japan 4%; these are issuer customer-region categories, not an assertion that end demand is located in the same countries. Fabless customers were 85%, IDMs 15%. [Q2 operating report, pp. 7–9](https://www.umc.com/upload/media/08_Investors/Financials/Quarterly_Results/Quarterly_2020-2029_English_pdf/2026/Q2_2026/UMC26Q2_report.pdf).

Q2 revenue was NT$68.733bn, gross margin 32.5%, operating margin 21.8%. Shipments increased 10.6% sequentially to 1.129m twelve-inch-equivalent wafers; quarterly capacity was 1.305m and utilization 85%. **Utilization is based on production, not shipments divided by capacity**, so do not recalculate it using the shipment denominator. ASP increased qualitatively; the issuer did not supply an exact percentage in the reviewed report. [Q2 operating report](https://www.umc.com/upload/media/08_Investors/Financials/Quarterly_Results/Quarterly_2020-2029_English_pdf/2026/Q2_2026/UMC26Q2_report.pdf).

The operating recovery is real, but reported net income is not recurring foundry cash earnings. Q2 parent net income of NT$42.260bn compares with operating income of NT$14.950bn. Equity-method profits were NT$23.606bn and other gains NT$6.054bn. H1 equity-method profit was NT$26.421bn, dominated by investment entities Hsun Chieh and Yann Yuan. Forecasting this as a foundry operating margin would be a serious category error. [June financial statements, income statement and note 6(7)/attachment 7](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).

## Ten-year record and capital intensity
The audited 2016–2025 series is supplied as original-as-filed and latest-comparative views, with 2,624 field observations, row/cell locators and source hashes. Revenue moved from NT$147.870bn in 2016 to NT$237.553bn in 2025, but the path was cyclical: 2022 reached NT$278.705bn and operating income NT$104.292bn; 2025 operating income was NT$43.949bn. Peak-cycle margins are not a perpetual default.

CFO less cash PP&E was negative in 2016 and 2023 and only about NT$5.3bn in 2024, before intangible spending and lease principal. It improved to approximately NT$52.1bn in 2025 as PP&E cash spending fell. This is not unlevered FCFF: CFO includes investment income, taxes and interest, and capex can be lumpy. H1 2026 CFO was NT$55.679bn, cash PP&E NT$21.349bn, cash intangibles NT$1.339bn and lease principal NT$0.420bn. That simple cash residual is about NT$32.570bn before removing nonoperating investment receipts and adjusting financing effects. [2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526193757/d91630d20f.htm), [June financials](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).

Comparability is explicitly limited by IFRS9/15 in 2018, IFRS16 in 2019, IAS37 amendments in 2022, the October 2019 USJC acquisition and the 2023 USCXM investor-obligation settlement. A 2021 deposit reclassification moved NT$28.835bn from other current assets to amortized-cost financial assets without changing total assets. The 2016 prepayment cash-flow aggregation likewise did not change CFO. These are documented presentation changes, not invented corrections. Historical dividend tables' “outstanding” share labels can include treasury shares; EPS averages and actual issued counts are kept separate. Read `history-methodology-v1.md` and `history-breaks-v1.json` before comparing ratios.

## Capacity, reinvestment and the forecast
Management raised 2026 capex from US$1.5bn to **US$2bn** and approved a **NT$148.68bn phased** Singapore/Tainan expansion budget. The board authorization is not an immediate cash bill and must not be added again on top of the cash-capex forecast. The plan combines Singapore cleanroom/tool expansion and a new Tainan building shell, with spending tied to customer commitments. Announced advanced technologies, silicon photonics and the Intel 12nm collaboration are opportunities, not booked incremental revenue in this DCF. The guidance anchors preserve the precise dated announcements and milestones. [July board announcements](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322027/umc-ex99.htm).

The three analyst operating cases use next-twelve-month revenue of NT$270/300/320bn and cash capex of NT$75/85/95bn, with explicit subsequent investment and margin paths. The base starts near the annualized Q3 monthly revenue sum; the capex cases exceed a simple US$2bn-at-June-FX translation to allow for expansion into 2027. These are judgmental scenarios, not management annual revenue guides or calibrated probability distributions. Cash capex includes settlement of prior equipment payables, intangible investment and existing construction/IP commitments. Leases are consistently normalized as operating rent: forecast pre-lease margins minus total lease cash, tax on that operating profit, and D&A excluding ROU depreciation. Terminal profits retain the grown lease cash cost and reinvest only in nonleased operating capital; no additional lease liability is deducted. Neither grants nor new customer financing is a free offset.

Terminal cash flow is constrained by both a 12% incremental-ROIC reinvestment formula and grown final-year FCFF, taking the lower. This prevents a free terminal capex reduction. WACC is 9.5–12% and perpetual growth 2–3% in nominal TWD; these are disclosed analyst risk assumptions, not price-fitted estimates.

## Guidance record and the latest information
The guidance package compares ten completed quarters, Q1 2024 through Q2 2026, using original prior guides. It keeps qualitative shipment/ASP language qualitative and does not invent precision from graphs. Q1 2026 ASP declined despite a firm outlook; Q2 2025 gross margin of 28.7% was below approximately 30% guidance. Shipment upside occurred in Q1/Q3 2024 and Q2 2026. Annual capex budgets, subsequent revisions and cash spending are separate fields, not an erroneous quarterly beat/miss score. Full issuer call transcripts were not located; reports, decks and call notices were frozen instead.

July, August and September monthly revenue sum to **NT$74.239117bn**, +8.01% sequentially and +25.56% year over year. This establishes quarterly sales from issuer monthly data, not Q3 margin, shipment or earnings outcomes. The Q3 results call is October 28, after the cutoff. Outstanding Q3 guidance is high-single-digit shipment growth, firm ASP, mid-30% gross margin and 90%+ utilization. [Monthly sales](https://www.umc.com/en/IR_Financial/monthly_sales_revenue), [quarterly archive](https://www.umc.com/en/Download/quarterly_results/QuarterlyResults).

An October filing explicitly declines comment on press speculation of 21% FY2026 revenue growth and 133% profit growth. Those are **not issuer guidance** and are excluded from the model. See the frozen October 13 exhibit in the guidance provenance.

## Taxes cannot be inferred from headline earnings
H1 tax expense includes an approximately NT$1.947bn deferred-tax benefit. Singapore's incentive extends to July 2035, while the renewed Taiwan–Singapore agreement begins January 2027 and its tax-sparing provision ends after three taxable years. UMC says this will increase future effective taxes, but supplies no exact normalized group ETR. Thus H1's roughly 5.64% headline ETR is not the terminal cash-tax rate. The scenarios explicitly use 20–25% on positive operating profit, no NOL refunds or DTA cash addback. The June DTL is not blindly deducted again: its operating/nonoperating partition is unresolved, operating cash taxes are already modeled, and no portfolio sale is assumed. [June financials, note 6(26), pp. 52–53](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm).

## Cash, deposits, debt and distribution claims
June cash was NT$124.706bn, plus NT$22.136bn of current time deposits with original maturities over three months. The latter is valued at face in the illustrated exclusion policy but is not spendable at inception; it converts to cash in the first annual funding bucket. This does not certify early withdrawal or geographic fungibility.

The financial debt proxy is NT$57.557bn, not total liabilities minus cash. The stricter policy reserves all bank principal up front. The separately modeled staged policy reserves sourced current bank principal of NT$6.402bn immediately and allocates all NT$11.490bn noncurrent bank principal to year 2, an explicitly conservative early-bucket assumption rather than an exact contractual annual schedule. Both reserve the residual Novatek redemption up front; domestic bonds follow their sourced maturity schedule. The Novatek bond exchanges into an investment holding, not UMC common shares. Current deposits, contract liabilities, refunds, taxes and declared dividends are accounted for in the same valuation and funding policy, never deducted twice. Customer capacity-reservation deposits of NT$40.674bn are not treated as permanent free cash. The NT$32.704bn declared dividend payable is deducted once for an **ex-declared-distribution** study; ordinary and ADS payments followed in July/August.

A further NT$1.908bn reserve covers legacy pension, decommissioning, onerous-contract and carbon-fee obligations, with no second forecast settlement charge. After that correction, the all-bank-upfront policy fails initial available liquidity by about NT$490m and remains withheld. The separately modeled staged-bank policy begins with about NT$11.000bn available liquidity and passes all three annual cash paths; this is not daily liquidity proof. The more demanding stress policy also fails and remains withheld. No future borrowing, post-June convertible proceeds, investment sales or new grants rescue that failed case.

## Why the investment portfolio is excluded, not called worthless
UMC has substantial direct financial investments and equity-accounted associates. Associates also hold UMC shares, including Hsun Chieh, SIS and Yann Yuan. Adding quoted stake values plus holding-company book values to a DCF can double count assets and introduce circular UMC ownership. Book value is not a substitute for realizable after-tax value. The capital package lists the actual portfolio, quoted values where disclosed and cross-holdings.

This initial calculator therefore assigns **zero incremental value to every nonoperating equity investment and no reduction of ordinary shares for circular holdings**. That is an explicit exclusion scenario, not an appraisal of those assets at zero and not a guaranteed valuation floor. Any full-company portfolio addback requires a separately reviewed look-through, tax, ownership and claim reconciliation. The engine rejects a nonzero portfolio addback to prevent an unsupported shortcut.

## Current targets remain unavailable
Post-June domestic convertibles produced approximately NT$16.913bn proceeds. An October announcement priced US$1.8bn overseas zero-coupon convertibles with distinct maturities, put rights, fixed conversion FX and initial conversion prices. June authorized-but-unissued financing is not cash at June 30, and later proceeds cannot be credited without matching liability/dilution. Later restricted-share cancellations likewise change current capital. The February 2026 authorization for up to67m new restricted ordinary shares is also included as an explicit maximum issuance scenario, in addition to June issued shares and without crediting proceeds. Actual issuance date is unverified; already-issued restricted shares are not added twice. Retained SBC expense can conservatively overlap the full award allocation, so this is not an exact fair compensation valuation. The capital addendum records these events; the dated model excludes post-June financing and cancellations transparently, while including the explicit 67m authorized-award scenario. All `current_target` fields remain null.
